findings.title: Pagination creates a phantom page for exact page-size member counts
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which returns 2 for a group with exactly 50 members and a limit of 50 (and similarly for every exact multiple). The Next control is therefore enabled and requests offset 50, producing an empty member page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (while retaining the zero-member special case) so the last populated page is correctly identified.

findings.title: Automatic groups still render a member removal control
findings.body: This item view's context is an individual `member`, so `automatic` is looked up on that user rather than on the group being edited. It will normally be undefined, making `unless automatic` true even for automatic groups. As a result, admins see a removable-x control for automatic-group members; clicking it sends a request that the server rejects. Pass the group's automatic state into the item view or conditionally render the entire member list/control from the parent group context.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded client-controlled page size
findings.body: `limit` is taken directly from the request and passed to ActiveRecord without a maximum. A request such as `?limit=1000000` can force serialization of an entire large group's membership in one response; on PostgreSQL, a negative LIMIT may also mean no limit. This public endpoint should clamp the value to a positive, bounded page size before querying to prevent expensive queries, excessive memory use, and oversized responses.
